title: OpsTruss daemon
description: daemon/<stack>.json: how to reach and stop the daemon of one stack, and the programs it guards. The daemon lives while it holds daemon/<stack>.lock, so the file outlives it. Readers ignore fields they do not know and refuse a newer version.

start.description: When the process started, as the system tells it; compared only with itself, on this host.

opstruss.description: The version of OpsTruss that the daemon runs.

socket.description: The control socket, in daemon/ or, when that path is too long for a Unix socket, under $TMPDIR.

processes.description: The programs that the daemon guards, each written before it runs, so the next daemon stops what is left of them.

id.description: OPSTRUSS_SERVICE_ID, which every process of the program carries.

pid.description: The leader of the program's session and process group.

start.description: When the leader started, as the system tells it.

lock.description: The lock that the program's processes inherit, relative to .opstruss.

listen.description: The address the webhooks listen on, with the port the system gave for :0.

schedules.description: The schedule and every triggers that the daemon installed: when each last made a run, which a persistent schedule catches up from, and when it comes next.

key.description: The hash of the cron and time zone, or of the interval, which names the trigger apart from its place in the list.
